text:
alex: Heads up — observed a customer get charged twice after a stream reconnect when KV was evicted mid-request. Console shows a provisional charge and then a confirmed charge that double-counts the same tokens.

alex: Repro snippets and log:```
INFO 2026-03-22T11:02:03Z request_id=r-0x9a7 stream_id=s-42 action=recv packets=12 kv_hit=false reconnect=true provisional_tokens=180 confirmed_tokens=360
WARN 2026-03-22T11:02:03Z ledger:emit provisional session_id=ss-71 provenance=resume origin=region-a
INFO 2026-03-22T11:02:05Z ledger:confirm session_id=ss-71 tokens=360 origin=initial
```

maria: Ugh. Can you paste the exact request/session metadata (headers) — we need to know which fields survive the reconnect.

alex: header dump: `x-session-id:ss-71`, `x-stream-restart:true`, `x-client-trace:r-9f2`. We currently set `origin` to `resume` on reconnect path, but the confirmed ledger entry still gets `origin=initial` from the broker.

sam: Sounds like a provenance mismatch between the stream router and ledger writer. The router marks resumed chunks as provisional under a resume provenance, then the confirmation path writes them as initial (or vice versa). That will show up as distinct ledger records and look like separate consumption.

lee: Right — we have two orthogonal IDs: session_id and client_trace. session_id gets reused on resume, client_trace sometimes rotates. If ledger joins on the wrong key we double count.

maria: Proposal: add a small, immutable provenance token (origin_trace_id) emitted at session creation and propagated through reconnects. Ledger would join by (origin_trace_id, sequence_range) when mapping provisional->confirmed. Minimal header change.

sam: Alternative: maintain a mapping in the routing layer that tracks provisional token ranges per session and annotates confirmations with a provisional_ref. But that requires routing state to be durable across failovers.

lee: I prefer the origin_trace_id — stateless for routing and small. Downside: header size + we need a migration plan for older clients.

alex: For visibility: console needs to surface provisional->confirmed mapping. Right now console shows two ledger rows with different "origin" and no obvious link. UX idea: show a collapsible view "Provisional snapshots" under request trace with a link to the confirming ledger entry.

maria: We should also add a telemetry metric: `provisional_unmatched_ratio` per route. Quick query:```sql
SELECT route, count(*) AS unmatched_provisional
FROM ledger_entries
WHERE type='provisional' AND confirmed_ref IS NULL AND created_at > now() - interval '7 days'
GROUP BY route
ORDER BY unmatched_provisional DESC;
```
This will catch regressions during rollout.

sam: For rollout: small canary (10%) on internal orgs + enable origin_trace_id header on client library 0.13.0. Routing will treat presence of header as authoritative mapping key. If header absent, fall back to existing behavior.

lee: Ops concern: we need to ensure the ledger lookup/join on (origin_trace_id, seq_range) is indexed — otherwise we risk latency spike on confirmations. Add DB index before flip.

alex: I'll open an RFC and attach a tiny console mock + SQL index patch. Also adding an automated reconciliation job that looks for provisional entries older than 1h and flags them for manual review.

maria: For immediate mitigation, we can run a retrospective reconcile for the affected tenant and issue a provisional refund. I'll coordinate with CS. :wave:

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary-health-checks -> in 30m (automated) :gear:

sam: One more nit: streaming retries that re-send already-ack'd tokens must include `x-origin-trace` so dedupe works if the client resends buffered chunks after a flaky network.

lee: agree. Also add a unit test that simulates KV eviction mid-request and asserts single ledger mapping.

alex: Thanks — I'll file the RFC and a small PR with the header, migration notes, and the console mock. Will ping when the RFC is up. :thumbsup:
